text:
Devon: Quick heads-up — Polaris POC next week. They asked for a one-page handoff: how we create hosted API keys for two engineers, rotation schedule, and how to run a revoke test. Can we put together a minimal playbook? cc @sam_se @nina_security
Sam_SE: TL;DR: use ephemeral scoped keys, deliver via 1Password/signed link, provide rotate API example, and document revoke test steps. How long will Polaris need access?
Devon: 10 days total. They prefer automated rotation every 24h but want the option to manually revoke during tests.
Eli_Platform: Proposed minimal playbook steps:
1) Create two ephemeral keys with 24h TTL, scopes limited to "generate" and "embeddings".
2) Deliver via one-time signed download link (15m validity) or push to their secrets manager.
3) Enable IP allowlist if they provide CIDRs and set per-key rate limits.
4) Configure audit export to their S3 bucket for the POC window.
5) Show how to run revoke test and collect logs.
Sam_SE: Example commands we can hand them:
```
# create ephemeral key
redwood-cli keys create --type ephemeral --expires-in 24h --scope generate,embed --note "polaris-poc-dev1"
# rotate programmatically
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SVC_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/:alias/rotate
# revoke instantly
redwood-cli keys revoke <key-id>
```
Nina_Security: Security checklist to include in playbook:
- TTL policy: 24h default during POC (ok to extend to 48h with approval)
- Delivery: 1Password entry or signed link; no client-side embedding
- Revocation: immediate via Console/CLI/API; document in runbook
- Auditability: Console logs + export to customer S3 (KMS recommended)
- Scope: least privilege only; avoid full-admin scopes
- Incident contact: security@redwood.ai
Devon: Polaris asked if Redwood can provide the rotate lambda example so their CI can call it and push to AWS Secrets Manager.
Eli_Platform: We have a tiny Lambda snippet in docs. Flow: service account (read-only to rotate endpoint) -> call /v1/keys/:alias/rotate -> push new secret to Secrets Manager. We'll add code sample and a minimal IAM policy to the playbook.
Deploy-bot: Internal link: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/keys-ephemeral (contains examples, rotate lambda, audit export)
Sam_SE: For the revoke test steps to give Polaris:
1) We provision keys and deliver.
2) They run a simple load script hitting the API.
3) On scheduled time we revoke key via CLI or Console.
4) Polaris confirms client requests start returning 401 and collects timestamps.
5) We verify audit log entry for revoke and share path to exported logs.
Devon: Any gotchas we should warn Polaris about?
Nina_Security: Note about caching: clients may cache credentials or reuse sockets. Recommend short-lived in-memory caches and immediate retry on 401 to fetch new creds. Also advise disabling aggressive connection reuse for the revoke test window.
Eli_Platform: Also include fallback guidance: if they need longer-lived tokens later, propose a Dedicated project token with RBAC + audit sink. For POC, stick to ephemeral.
Devon: Great, I'll assemble the one-page playbook (handoff checklist + revoke test procedure + SecQ snippets) and share for review. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
